title: Q6 v2: orchestrator/planner_shadow.py + .mcp.planner-shadow.json — non-mutating Opus shadow Planner launches, structured result parsing, agreement scoring (P6)
spec:
Why: the brief (P6) requires shadow mode where Fable stays the production Planner and an Opus shadow decision is recorded without any production effect. goals.launch_planner (goals.py:322-353) and planner_runs.launch_routed give the headless Planner the full MCP surface (.mcp.planner.json: orchestrator, bus, github) and all tools, so a shadow launch through them could mutate the bus, plan.md or git. (v2 only rewords v1 T-0684: its spec quoted the template placeholder literally, which breaks spawn.render.)
What: new module orchestrator/planner_shadow.py and new file .mcp.planner-shadow.json whose content is a JSON object with an empty mcpServers map. The prompt template .orchestrator/prompts/planner-shadow.md already exists on goal/T-0674 and has one placeholder named packet; render it with spawn.render("planner-shadow", packet=text). Do not edit any prompt file.
- RouterDecision comes from orchestrator/planner_router.py (merged on goal/T-0674): fields tier, mode, hard, hold, hold_reason, reasons, hard_reasons, soft_score, shadow_tier, candidates, evidence, decision_type; cfg is planner_router.load_cfg(pool_cfg) with key shadow_sample_rate.
- eligible(router_decision, cfg, *, sample) -> (bool, reason): True only when router_decision.mode == "shadow", router_decision.shadow_tier is not None, router_decision.hold is False and sample <= cfg["shadow_sample_rate"]; reasons in order: mode_not_shadow, held, no_shadow_tier (covers hard decisions, whose shadow_tier is None), sampled_out, eligible.
- argv(prompt, *, model, budget_usd, system_prompt_path) -> list: ["claude", "-p", prompt, "--model", model, "--output-format", "json", "--max-budget-usd", str(budget_usd), "--mcp-config", ".mcp.planner-shadow.json", "--strict-mcp-config", "--disallowedTools", "Edit,Write,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit,Bash,Task,WebFetch,WebSearch", "--append-system-prompt", text of system_prompt_path (the caller passes .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md), "--dangerously-skip-permissions"]; no bus/orchestrator MCP server, no write tools.
- launch(prompt, *, model, account, budget_usd, log, root=ROOT, popen=None) -> {"pid", "log", "stderr_log", "argv"} or None on any exception (message to stderr, never raised; the production launch must not be affected). Env: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from account.config_dir, ORCH_ROOT, ORCH_SHADOW=1, oauth token like goals.launch_planner; never resolve [secrets.planner] (a shadow has no GitHub or Jev access). popen defaults to goals.Popen so tests inject a fake; start_new_session=True; stdout to log, stderr to log + ".stderr". Budget: the caller passes [limits].max_budget_usd.planner_shadow (default 1.5).
- parse(log_path) -> dict or None: last JSON line of the log, take its "result" text, spawn.extract_json (orchestrator/spawn.py:646) it, whitelist keys proposed_action (one of fix_round, respec, escalate, noop, synthesize_now, wait_for_more, drop_low_confidence, write_specs, close, other; anything else -> other), summary (cap 800 chars, jev.redact applied), tasks_proposed (list of {title (cap 120), scope (list cap 10)} cap 10), confidence (float clamped 0-1 or None), needs_fable (bool), unresolved (list of str cap 10, each cap 200); plus usage via bus.normalize_usage("claude", usage), total_cost_usd, session_id, is_error. Anything else dropped; a missing/non-JSON result -> {"parse_error": True, plus the usage fields}; unreadable log -> None.
- record(*, launch_id, goal_id, decision_type, state_version, model, tier, started_at, parsed, latency_s, root=None) -> row appended to root/runs/sched/planner_shadow.jsonl (write the file directly like planner_telemetry does; no schedlog global swap) without prompt text.
- score(shadow_row, production_materiality) -> {"agreement": True|False|None, "basis", "needs_fable_matched": True|False|None}: production action derived from planner_telemetry's materiality shape: fix_round when fix_strategy_for non-empty; write_specs when new_tasks non-empty and fix_strategy_for empty (shadow synthesize_now counts as agreeing with write_specs); escalate when escalated; noop when nothing material; agreement None when production_materiality is None or shadow parse_error; needs_fable_matched compares shadow needs_fable with production_materiality.get("reescalated") when present, else None.
- summary(root=None) -> {"n", "agreement_rate", "needs_fable_rate", "parse_error_rate", "usd", "tokens"} tolerant of malformed lines.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_shadow.py::test_argv_has_no_bus_mcp_and_no_write_tools — argv uses .mcp.planner-shadow.json (whose file content has an empty mcpServers map), --strict-mcp-config, a --disallowedTools list containing Edit, Write and Bash, the shadow model, and never .mcp.planner.json

tests/test_planner_shadow.py::test_launch_failure_is_isolated_and_production_unchanged — a popen that raises makes launch return None without raising; the bus tasks directory and plan.md hash are identical before and after a successful fake launch; env carries ORCH_SHADOW=1 and no secrets.planner values

tests/test_planner_shadow.py::test_parse_whitelists_and_caps — a log whose result JSON has proposed_action fix_round, a 3000-char summary, 15 tasks and an extra transcript key parses to summary 800 chars, 10 tasks, no transcript; a non-JSON result gives parse_error True with usage still read

tests/test_planner_shadow.py::test_score_agreement_against_production_materiality — shadow fix_round vs production fix_strategy_for gives agreement True; shadow escalate vs production new_tasks gives False; shadow synthesize_now vs new_tasks gives True; missing materiality gives None

tests/test_planner_shadow.py::test_eligible_and_summary — eligible is False with reasons mode_not_shadow, held, no_shadow_tier and sampled_out for the matching RouterDecision inputs and True for a shadow decision; summary over three rows including one malformed line reports n and rates without raising

constraints.interface_contract: eligible(router_decision, cfg, *, sample) -> (bool, reason); argv(prompt, *, model, budget_usd, system_prompt_path) -> list; launch(prompt, *, model, account, budget_usd, log, root, popen) -> {pid, log, stderr_log, argv}|None; parse(log_path) -> whitelisted dict|None; record(*, launch_id, goal_id, decision_type, state_version, model, tier, started_at, parsed, latency_s, root) -> row in runs/sched/planner_shadow.jsonl; score(shadow_row, production_materiality) -> {agreement, basis, needs_fable_matched}; summary(root). RouterDecision from planner_router (fields mode, shadow_tier, hold). Wave B calls eligible/launch/parse/record/score from planner_runs.run_group and reconcile.

result.summary: superseded by Q6 v3 after spec review request_changes (needs_fable_matched compares against materiality['escalated'], the key planner_telemetry.materiality actually emits; acceptance exercises the present and absent cases)

spec_review_risks.issue: score()'s needs_fable_matched is specified to read production_materiality.get("reescalated"), but planner_telemetry.materiality() (the only producer of the 'materiality shape' the spec cites) never emits a "reescalated" key — it emits "escalated" (planner_telemetry.py:188-191). The only reescalation-named field in the codebase is "reescalation", a boolean on a different jsonl schema (planner_invocations launch rows, planner_telemetry.py:88), not part of materiality()'s output. As specified, needs_fable_matched will always fall through to None for every real caller, silently disabling the metric it exists to compute. No acceptance test in the packet exercises a 'reescalated present' case (test_score_agreement_against_production_materiality only checks agreement, not needs_fable_matched), so an executor implementing this literally will ship dead code that passes all listed tests.
